recipes.name: Pork Chop and Cabbage Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13 baking dish.
Place a layer of shredded cabbage into baking dish and then a layer of sliced potatoes. Repeat cabbage and potatoes and salt.
Simmer the soup, water and diced onion. Pour over cabbage and potatoes.
In a skillet, brown each pork chop in a small amount of oil and place on top of mixture. Bake for 1 1/2 hours uncovered or until chops are tender.

raw_recipe.headline: Pork Chop and Cabbage Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Baked pork chops, cabbage and potatoes with a creamy chicken sauce.

review.reviewBody: This was really good. I cut the recipe in half since there is just two of us. It worked out well. I used milk with the soup rather than water, I also used cream of mushroom. I added pepper and garlic powder when I was layering the cabbage and potatoes. I also sprinkled salt, pepper, and garlic powder on the chops before I browned them. I used cooking spray rather than oil. Our chops were a bit dry, but not too bad. I think next time I would either cover the dish to prevent the chops from drying out, or pour the soup over the top of the chops too.

Hello everyone it's Dine-In with DY here, and hope everybody's having a great evening. I just wanted to post a quick review of this fantastic recipe that I came across with my alterations. I love the simplicity of the recipe but found myself without pork chops on hand so substituted with boneless chicken thighs and adjusted the flavor profile accordingly. I used cream of chicken condensed soup rather than cream of mushroom, and used milk instead of water when mixing the soup. I also added green bell pepper in addition to the onions as the soup thickened. I also included a tablespoon of sugar to offset some of the saltiness. I layered the cabbage and potatoes per the recipe but added some salt and pepper between the layers for flavor. Tip: for evenly layered potatoes, use a mandalin. I also increased the temperature to 400? and baked the cabbage and potatoes along with the soup mixture for half an hour, then added the chicken which I diced and rubbed with a favorite chicken rub. I then covered with tin foil cooking an additional hour. I also introduced some mozzarella cheese to this dish which the recipe did not call for. 15 minutes before the cooktime was complete, I uncovered and and added the mozzarella cheese and continued baking For an additional 15 minutes.. It turned out divine. Thank you so much. Will be making again and sharing the recipe for sure! As the final thought, if you find yourself without pork chops or chicken, another great substitute for a protein

This is a fantastic recipe. I would have given it five stars, but the part about leaving it all uncovered while it bakes does not work. I tightly covered it with aluminum foil until the last 20 minutes. The pork chops were not dry or tough as many have experienced. It was all well-blended, moist, and baked to perfection. I always double recipes even though it's just my husband and myself. The leftovers are very good as the flavors enhance even more later. This is great served with maple glazed carrots and biscuits.

We enjoyed this. SO doesn't like any thing too spicy , so this was perfect . I had to change the cooking method a little , as I shredded too much cabbage . I used a 11x15 baking dish , and layered cabbage , potatoes , and diced onion , s&p in the bottom of the dish . Since I had so much cabbage , I doubled the soup and water . I poured 1/2 of it over the layer of veggies . ( warmed up ) Repeated layers . The dish was full , so I popped it in the oven for 30 min. uncovered . Put the browned chops on top after the 30 mins. and covered the dish . Baked for 30 more mins. then uncovered the dish for 15 more mins. We will have this dish again .

Vegetarian Slow Cooker revision: I used the "ingredient search" for the vegetables that I had on hand: cabbage, potatoes and onions, and this recipe came up. It sounded like it would be good, even without the meat, and it was! I used cream of mushroom soup (instead of chicken), and based on others' suggestions: seasoned salt, pepper, garlic powder and sprinkled a little celery seed over each layer. Instead of baking I just layered all in my slow cooker, on high for 4 hours. Great side dish!

This was really very delicious! I didn’t have cream of chicken soup so I just used 10oz of chicken broth and dotted the cabbage layer with a little butter to add richness. I did follow the recommendation of another review and I baked the cabbage/potato part for 30 minutes uncovered at 400, then I added the browned pork chops, covered, and baked for 1:15 at 350. The pork chops were tender and delicious. Great comfort food recipe.

This was phenomenal! I did spice it up by adding 1/2 thinly sliced apple, crumbled bacon and chicken broth instead of water. Plus, when layering I added Penzey’s Sunny Paris seasoning (my go-to salt substitute). My hubby is already asking for me to make this again! Perfect on a cold night!

I read reviews for ideas beforehand. I put a medium sliced onion directly on the layers of cabbage/potatoes. I used a can each of Cream of Mushroom & Chicken soup; one soup can of milk and poured it over the pork chops once assembled. I seasoned the pork chops well & dredged them in a little flour before frying lightly in a little oil. I covered the dish for the 1st hour; uncovered the last half hour. Great taste but unfortunately, no amount of steaming was going to make these chops tender.

Oh yum! I made a lot of changes based on other reviews. I added thin sliced carrots and rough diced onions. Dotted with butter and used chicken broth. Seasoned veggies with onion powder, paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper. Baked covered at 400 for 30 mins. Put the browned 1.5 inch thick pork chops with bacon slices on top at 375 for 20 mins. Perfect and delicious!! A keeper for sure.
It was delicious! I did use milk instead of water with the soup, made it like a creamy gravy. I also did cover it after a while, but the chops did not dry out. Hubs loved it too. :-)

I used a seasoning salt and pepper as I browned the chops. Used cream of mushroom and added a few slice baby bella mushrooms and sliced onions. Covered with foil which I removed after about 50 minutes and baked for 10 minutes more. Chops were moist and veggies were very done. If you cover and if the chops are essentially cooked during the browning, you can take 30 minutes off the cook time (unless your veggies are in a really thick layer. Very good way to use extra cabbage and adaptable to other veggie additions and seasonings.

So easy to modify...cream of chicken works but so does cream of mushroom, cream of broccoli and I chop and add a head of broccoli too.This lacks real flavor.. add savory paprika, garlic... It needs something.

I was really disappointed in this recipe as it is very similar to a recipe my mom made when I was young that I loved. However, I guess I should have read the reviews of other people before trying this one. It is in dire need of seasoning which I just noticed other people had mentioned also, and my thought was to use milk instead of water with the soup, which another reviewer suggested. I don't think I will make it again as it is too time consuming for the outcome.
Made it !! really good fall comfort food!!
This was delicious! I cut the recipe in half. I used Cream of Celery soup instead of the Cream of Chicken. My husband had seconds. There were no leftovers.

Pork chops were dray, although I cooked only an hour. Next time will do pork chops and potatoes with cabbage separately. I’m not a great cook but this should have been simple. Not moist enough and cabbage overcooked. Will not do this again.
Made this pretty much the same but used chicken as pork has been hard to find lately.
will definitely make again. Hubby said it was great.
